laws.historical_context: Enacted on September 23, 1946, shortly after Lebanese independence. Based on French labor law traditions. Has undergone numerous amendments to adapt to changing economic and social conditions. The 2010 amendment (Law 129/2010) was significant for Palestinian refugee workers.

laws.historical_context: Established the National Social Security Fund (CNSS/NSSF) in 1963. Created a social insurance system covering family allowances, sickness and maternity, and end-of-service indemnity. Major reform in December 2023 with Law 319 introducing a pension system to replace the end-of-service indemnity.

laws.historical_context: Landmark reform passed after 20+ years of discussions. Replaces the end-of-service indemnity (EOSI) lump-sum system with a lifelong pension based on notional defined contribution (NDC). Addresses the severe underfunding of the previous system and provides old-age income security. Approximately 80% of elderly Lebanese were not receiving any pension before this reform.
